title: How do we find the area of a pentagon?
description: A five sided shape is a rectangle six centimetres by four with a triangle three centimetres tall on its six centimetre side. A line splits it into a rectangle and a triangle, and the two areas add up to thirty three square centimetres. Keeko doubts the answer of forty two.
teaching_notes: One idea: split a polygon into a rectangle and a triangle, find each area, and add. Watch for students who treat the whole shape as one tall rectangle.

source: A pentagon is a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle with a triangle of he
video_script.why: The child can find the areas of rectangles and triangles, and here meets a five sided shape made of both, which a line splits into known pieces.
video_script.substitution: the book's pentagon as a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle with a triangle of height 3 cm on its 6 cm side
video_script.anchor: the book's five sided shape: a rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm with a triangle of height 3 cm on its 6 cm side
video_script.wrong_answer: six times seven, which is forty two
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes the full height of seven and says six times seven, which is forty two. That fills in the two empty corners beside the triangle, nine square centimetres too much.
video_script.payoff_line: The area is thirty three square centimetres
maths_rules: triangle on the 6 cm side, height 3 cm: 1/2 × 6 × 3 = 9 cm²
Keeko: full height 4 + 3 = 7; 6 × 7 = 42; 42 − 33 = 9 cm² of empty corners (the outer rectangle 6 × 3 = 18 minus the triangle 9)
video_script.design: One five sided shape all video. A line splits it into a rectangle and a triangle and the two areas are added. Keeko's doubt: one tall rectangle.

<bookmark mark='rect'/>Step one, find the area of the rectangle, length times breadth.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Six times four is twenty four square centimetres.

<bookmark mark='calc'/>Half of six times three is nine square centimetres.

<bookmark mark='add'/>Add twenty four and nine to get thirty three.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The area is thirty three square centimetres.
